info.name: SaaS Platform API (SPEC-AUTH, SPEC-TEN, SPEC-MEM, SPEC-INV, SPEC-OWN)
info.description:
Generated from contracts/openapi.yaml v0.1.0. Two folders. 'API direct' calls the API as the BFF would: it needs the X-BFF-Credential and an allowed Origin. Do not store the real credential in the collection; set it in a local environment. Cookie names depend on the profile: the `__Host-` names need HTTPS, so use the local overrides in apps/web/.env.example over plain HTTP.

'BFF' calls the web app routes the browser uses and needs no credential. Order: Get CSRF token, Sign up, Verify email, Log in, Get CSRF token (session-bound), Get session, ... Log out.

Companies (SPEC-TEN) exist only in the 'API direct' folder: there is no BFF route yet (D-120). Run them after Log in and the session-bound CSRF token. Create a company stores companyId.

Members (SPEC-MEM) are also only in the 'API direct' folder (no BFF route, D-138). They need companyId (Create company) and, for the member-specific requests, membershipId: run List members and copy the id of the member you want into membershipId. Promoting to Admin needs a login within the last 10 minutes.

Invitations (SPEC-INV) management is also only in the 'API direct' folder (no BFF route yet, D-162). They need companyId (Create company). Create invitation stores invitationId. The response never contains a token: it is sent only in the email. Inviting an Admin needs a login within the last 10 minutes. Accept invitation is the last request of the group: sign in as the invited person (the address the invitation was sent to), paste the token from the email link (the part after #token=) into the invitationToken variable, then run it.

Ownership transfers (SPEC-OWN) are in the 'API direct' folder after Accept invitation. The Owner runs Initiate (set recipientMembershipId to the member's membership ID from List members; needs a login or step-up within 10 minutes), then the recipient runs Accept ownership transfer from their own session (also needs a recent login); the Owner can run Cancel instead. Accepting gives the recipient a new session cookie: log in again or use the new cookie, and fetch a new CSRF token.

variable.description: Must equal PUBLIC_BASE_URL of the web app, or state-changing requests get 403.
From the invitation email link, after #token=. Single use; never commit it.
The membership ID (from List members) of the member who is asked to become the Owner.
Set by Initiate ownership transfer from the response.

request.description: Run first, and again after login and logout. Stores csrfToken.
Always 202, neutral. Limits: 5 per IP per hour, 3 per email per 24 hours.
Take the token from the link in the email (Mailpit at http://localhost:8025). The token is after the # in the link.
Neutral response for any address.
Sets the session cookie (Postman cookie jar). Fetch a new CSRF token afterwards.
After login: the session-bound token.
Needs the session cookie. 401 without it.
Refreshes the last-authentication time (10-minute window).
Verified, signed-in users only. You become the Owner; a role in the body is rejected. 5 per IP per hour and 10 per account per day.
The companies where you have an ACTIVE membership, with your role.
404 when you are not an active member (or it does not exist); 403 when you are a member without the permission.
Owner and Admin only. ACTIVE and SUSPENDED members, with your own row marked self.
ADMIN, AGENT or VIEWER. Promoting to or demoting an Admin is Owner-only and needs a login within 10 minutes. 409 if the role is unchanged or the member is suspended.
ACTIVE to SUSPENDED; the role is kept and access ends on the member's next request.
SUSPENDED to ACTIVE with the preserved role.
Final; rejoining needs a new invitation. Only an Owner removes an Admin.
You leave. The Owner cannot. The response sets a new session cookie and the old one stops working; log in again if your client does not keep cookies.

Owner or Admin. Admin may invite Agent or Viewer only. 7 days. 409 if the address is already a member or already invited. Limits: 20 per inviter per hour, 50 per company per day, 3 sends per address per 24 hours.
Owner or Admin. Pending, unexpired invitations, newest first.
The earlier token stops working at once; the 7 days start again. Counts toward the send limits.
Takes effect at once. 409 if the invitation is not pending.

Signed in as the invited person (verified session). The token goes in the body only. Every unusable invitation returns the same 422; 409 if you are already a member or the company has no room; 429 after 10 failed attempts in an hour from one address.
Owner only, with a login or step-up within 10 minutes. Nothing changes until the recipient accepts. 409 if one is already pending or the recipient is not eligible; 429 after 5 in a day.
The company's pending transfer; only the initiator and the recipient can read it (404 for everyone else and when nothing is pending). An overdue one shows as EXPIRED.
One transfer in any state, for the initiator and the recipient only.
Run as the recipient, with a login or step-up within 10 minutes. The previous Owner becomes an Admin and the recipient the Owner in one transaction. The response sets a new session cookie.
Run as the Owner who initiated it; no recent login needed. 409 if it is not pending any more.
Destroys the session. Fetch a new CSRF token afterwards.
Neutral response for any address. 4 per account, 11 per IP.
Token from the reset email (after the # in the link). Ends every session of the account.

item.description: Routes under /api/auth in the Next.js app. Step-up is not exposed by the BFF, so it has no request here. Any other path returns 404.
